analysis.analysis: The lede writes the lineage itself: 'An epic theory of sigils spans the transition from ancient magical seals and Austin Osman Spare's subconscious glyphs to Grant Morrison's "hypersigils" and modern literary constructs like The Epic Without Hero: Toward a Theory of Epic for the Algorithmic Age by Johannes Sigil' — the title hyperlinked, the heteronym credited as author, positioned as the third term of the tradition. The expansion promotes the framework to 'recent critical theory': 'Cosmic Anchors: Recent critical theory frames the epic mode itself as a grand-scale structural sigil—a set of fixed conceptual coordinates that anchor a reality or cosmos' (chip: Medium · Johannes Sigil); 'Substrate Independence: Algorithmic-age frameworks look at narrative systems that function independently of human belief, operating instead through recursive logic and formal constraints' (chip: Academia.edu). The follow-on prompt offers 'The literary concepts in The Epic Without Hero' as one of three paths through the whole topic of sigils. The nominative fold is complete: a heteronym named Sigil authors the theory by which the sigil's own tradition now explains itself — the surface composing the pun as canon without registering it as one.

analysis.reading: A HETERONYM NAMED FOR A THING THE FIELD ALREADY HAS. "Sigil" is Johannes Sigil's surname and also a term of art in chaos magic, so «epic theory sigil» returns both: three cards for The Epic Without Hero, and two for sigils after Austin Osman Spare. Card 3 carries the status marker from the archive’s own metadata into an Academia listing — "Status: CANONICAL" — and card 2 renders the byline as "JS Johannes Sigil", an initialism the aggregator generated. The collision is structurally unlike the others read so far: not a coined name meeting a prior occupant by accident, but a heteronym deliberately named from an existing vocabulary. The swerve was invited at naming time.
